extra.reason: Subsumed by keyfence-sut, which is the same idea done properly: credentials stored under operator-defined names, resolved through a backend, and token issuance taking a reference. keyfence-bmf now depends on sut instead.

Fixed in cdc80e0's successor (this commit): empty permits nothing, POST /tokens refuses an omitted or empty list with 400, and ['*'] is the explicit way to ask for an unrestricted token. The SSH bastion refuses a wildcard too. Nine unit tests, one verified to fail against the old behaviour; scripts/test.sh asserts the refusal.

Fixed: upstream hosts are authenticated against <data-dir>/ssh/known_hosts (or -ssh-known-hosts), unknown hosts and mismatched keys are refused with distinct messages and audit deny rules, the file is read per session, and -ssh-insecure-host-keys is the deliberate waiver. Six tests with real ed25519 keys. The ssh socket unit's warning is removed.
Examples, the demo and the example README now create a podman secret and pass -api-key-file /run/secrets/api-key. One deliberate -api-key example remains in the README, labelled as visible in /proc.
gofmt -l is clean across the repository, and CI fails if it stops being.

Root cause was not the network: the suite hardcoded 10210/10212 and was silently testing a running keyfence service with the wrong CA. Test ports moved to 10310-10312 with a refusal if taken; upstream reachability probed once with two tests skipped when it is not there; tests 2 and 7 no longer assert on a model name (they GET /v1/models); test 4 issues its own token instead of borrowing test 2's. Fourteen pass with network, twelve pass and two skip without.

Credentials can be registered by name (in $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY, -credentials-dir, or KEYFENCE_CREDENTIAL_<NAME>) and referenced at issuance with credential_ref. Resolved per request, so rotation is replacing a file. Names are validated as names, not paths; unknown refs are refused at issuance with the available list. Verified end to end against api.anthropic.com.

Credential material is forgotten once no valid token refers to it: immediately on explicit revoke, and on a one-minute sweep for expired tokens (Store.Cleanup existed and nothing called it). Shared credentials survive until the last token goes; certs and SSH keys are reaped the same way. A credential registered by name is never copied at all.
